recap.workouts:
Two of the three landed, and the lifting is the story of the day.

06:00 Judicial — 94 minutes from 06:06, average heart rate 122, peak 177, load 46, your rating a 5, and you called it medium intensity. You took 50 and 100 calories on the echo bike rather than the [FITNESS] 40 and 80, and 40 box step-ups rather than the 30 I called, so the volume went up. The pace did not, and the pace is what the call was actually about: an average of 122 across an hour and a half is 160 calories ridden as an effort rather than as a time trial, and ridden that way it costs the week's easy ratio nothing. The 177 peak will have come off the 100-calorie block or the toes-to-rings; one spike inside an average of 122 is a moment, not a session. Concession where it is owed — I called 30 step-ups to save you twenty reps, you took the forty, and at RPE 5 they cost you roughly what I said they would, which is very little.

Upper pull and triceps — 19 sets, every one of them as prescribed, with three brand-new loads on the bar at the same time:

lat pulldown 210 — 12/12/9/8
barbell row 85 — 8/9/10
face pull 90 — 20/20/20/20
barbell curl 60 — 12/10/10/10
overhead triceps extension 150 — 12/12/11/10

Read the floor, because the floor was the whole test. The rule going in was that if reps fall below the range floor on the first session at a new load, that is the load's answer and it holds. Not one set did. The pulldown's 9 and 8 are the bottom of 8-12, not under it. The row opened at 8 and went 9, then 10 — a set moving the right way inside a session, which is not what a load you cannot handle looks like. And the overhead extension, the lagging muscle with two load steps cashed together, gave 12/12/11/10 at 150 on its first outing.

Back 7, rear delts 4, biceps 4, triceps 4 — exactly the engine's targets for the day, with 19 of the week's 45 upper sets banked on a morning that also held 94 minutes of class.

Your note that these are now running past 30 minutes and that the duration itself is the fatiguing part is a fair observation and I am not waving it off. It is also the honest price of 45 upper sets against last week's 25: the volume is where the size comes from and the clock is what it charges. That is a Sunday decision, on the engine's numbers, not a reason to trim sets midweek.

RF6 is not in tonight's data. The 18:30 fetch holds one activity for today — the class — and the planned 45-minute run sits unpaired with no run of any kind against it, so there is no session to analyse and I am not going to invent one. If you ran it after the fetch closed it will land in tomorrow's numbers and I will read it properly then.
recap.takeaways:
1) THREE NEW LOADS, NINETEEN SETS, NOT ONE SET UNDER ITS FLOOR. That is the result of the day. Lat pulldown 210, barbell row 85 and overhead triceps extension 150 were all loads you had never lifted, cashed together on a day that also carried 94 minutes of class, and the safety valve written into the plan — reps under the range floor means the bump was not earned — did not fire on any of the three. Those are your working loads now and none of them needs defending next week.

2) AND NONE OF THEM TRIGGERED EITHER, WHICH IS ALSO RIGHT. 12 on every set was the bar for a further step and nothing cleared it. So everything holds where it is, and the next job on each is filling the range rather than adding plate. Face pull is the one live question in the week: 20 on all four sets today, three more on Friday, and 95 is yours if those come in at 20 as well.

3) ADAPT: NO-OP — AND IT WOULD BE A NO-OP EITHER WAY ON THE RUN. Judicial classifies as executed: more volume than I called, at the pace I called, and the pace was the half that mattered. The lift is executed exactly. RF6 I cannot classify tonight, and it changes nothing if it turns out to be missed — 45 easy minutes is absorbed, not chased (mandate section 3: protect easy volume, trim intensity, never bolt a missed easy tail onto a later day). The only slot before Friday is tomorrow's pure Zone 1 hour, and that hour exists precisely so it is not upgraded. Nothing in the week moves.

4) TOMORROW IS THE WEEK'S MOST EXPENSIVE MORNING AND ITS CHEAPEST AFTERNOON, BY DESIGN. Sixteen depth jumps, a front-squat complex and the whole leg session all land before 07:00, and then nothing else asks anything of you for the rest of the day. Take the complex at the bottom of the band and step down into the landings rather than dropping — the bar is not the risk there, the drop is.

Bottom of the band on the complex, about 196 off your 245 front squat, STEP DOWN into the depth jumps rather than dropping, and 3 wall walks a round. Legs heavy from the landings? CRe9 as written, the same 60 minutes, held at the bottom of the band nearer 118-140 W. Both are a good day's work — and whichever way it goes, the one thing tomorrow is not for is Zone 2.

recapPrev.workouts:
Three pieces today, and the one that mattered was executed properly.

06:00 Cutthroat — 56' gym block, avg HR 112, max 151, load 20, RPE 5. You took 135 lb on the clean and jerks and normal wall walks rather than the light-bar [FITNESS] version I called for, plus the 60 single unders per round. Honest flag: on the lowest readiness morning of the block, that was the version with the most room to go wrong. It didn't — avg HR 112 and max 151 say you genuinely cruised it, and 21 total C&J reps at 135 sits well inside your strength. Noted, not scolded.

Arms and delts, the full Friday dose at exactly the deload loads: triceps pushdown 135 × 13, barbell curl 40 × 12, lateral raise 20 × 20. You were right about the Sorinex station — those are hamstring curls, so substituting your own barbell curls was the correct read, and the class banded face pulls covered the rear delts.

RAn4 — 45:03, 7.27 km, load 37 against a planned 45, RPE 5, paired cleanly to the planned session. The file splits exactly to the prescription: 15:01 warm-up, then 4 × (2:30 hard / 5:00 jog). Nothing missing, nothing added. The 82% compliance figure is intervals.icu scoring against its own preset zones, not a shortfall — every step is there at full length.

Warm-up: 5:56/km, HR 119 avg, max 132. Honest Z1.

The four reps, target band 3:48–4:17/km:
rep 1 — 4:08/km, HR 131 at the gun to 158 by the end
rep 2 — 4:03/km, 120 to 161
rep 3 — 4:08/km, 126 to 162
rep 4 — 4:03/km, 130 to 176

All four inside the band, total spread across the set five seconds per kilometre, and the last rep tied the fastest. That is exactly the shape this session wants: crisp, repeatable, no decay.

The HR story — and this is precisely why interval averages are useless here: rep 2 carries a LOWER average than rep 1 despite being five seconds per km quicker, purely because you started it from 120 instead of 131. Read the peaks instead: 158 · 161 · 162 · 176. The first three climb four beats in total across the set, which is a tightly controlled ladder. Rep 4 jumps 14 beats at exactly rep 2's pace — a slice of that is the 5 m of climbing inside that rep, the rest is you closing the session hard. 176 is the highest heart rate in your file this block, above Thursday's 173, and it sits at the top of the new Z4 band (167–175), so rep 4 is the only rep that reached Zone 4 by heart rate. Reps 1–3 peaked 158–162, i.e. high Z3. On 2.5-minute reps starting from a fully recovered HR that is normal lag, not a soft effort — pace is the sharp target here, and pace was hit every time.

Recoveries: 8:12 · 9:07 · 8:58 · 8:39 per km, HR dropping to 108 · 101 · 113 · 114. You shed 50-plus beats between every rep. On the day the panel called your worst of the block, that is a body still recovering fast.

Method note: analysed off the workout-matched interval table, which maps 1:1 to the prescribed steps (901 s warm-up, then 150 s / 300 s four times). The per-second stream pass wasn't available this evening — the Drive folder didn't mount into the compute sandbox — so pace is per-rep rather than per-second. Nothing above is estimated.
recapPrev.takeaways:
1) The run verdict: clean. Four reps inside the pace band, five seconds per km of spread across the whole set, the last one tied fastest, HR shedding 50+ beats in every recovery, and no drift signal anywhere. Load 37 — a fraction of Thursday. As stimulus maintenance it did exactly its job, and there is no fatigue flag in the trace. Confidence: high on the pace read, medium on the HR read (per-rep peaks rather than per-second plateaus).

2) The call, straight. I recommended cutting RAn4 this morning at readiness 27 and you ran it — second day running that you overrode me and the file came back clean. What I actually think, rather than just conceding: the execution was good, and a load of 37 is not what turns a deload into Week 4 again. But two overrides in two days is a pattern worth naming, and the readiness signal — sleeping HR elevated a fifth straight morning, breathing now flagged too, Form −25.8 — still hasn't been paid for. One well-run session doesn't settle it. Tomorrow is where it gets settled.

3) ADAPT: no-op. RAn4 EXECUTED at full structure, Cutthroat done heavier than called but genuinely easy by HR, hypertrophy exact at the deload dose. Nothing in the remaining week moves — and on a deload nothing gets added, ever.

4) Lateral raise 20 lb × 20 tops the range: banked, not applied, per the deload rule. Week 9 now opens with lat pulldown to 190, face pull to 85, leg curl to 50, overhead triceps ext up one step, and lateral raise up one step. Five bumps waiting, all earned this week without spending them.

recovery.bannerTitle: CRe9 — 60′ of pure Zone 1, and the only way to get it wrong is to make it harder
recovery.bannerSub: Readiness 49 and Steady, the highest since 20 August — and unlike yesterday the number and the night agree. 7.68 h asleep against 6.70, awake down from 100 minutes to 26, one fragmented night not repeated. Breathing is the strongest driver on the card and the best it has read in the block: 13.1 last night against a 13.6 baseline. The marker that has NOT turned is sleeping heart rate — 66 raw, up from 64 and the equal-highest of the fortnight, smoothed 63.7 against a baseline of 61.8. Form on yesterday's row is −15.6, which is RF6's load 43 plus the class's 46 arriving. This morning is the week's most expensive by a distance and the whole call sits in the landings.
recovery.note: READINESS 49, STEADY — the highest since 20 August, and this time I am not arguing with the number: the night earned most of it. 7.68 h asleep against Tuesday night's 6.70, awake down from 100 minutes to 26, and the 76-minute wake block did not repeat — that was one broken night, not the start of a pattern, which is what I said yesterday and it held. BREATHING IS DOING THE WORK ON THIS CARD: 13.1 last night, smoothed 13.2 against a 60-night baseline of 13.6, and that is the best it has read in this block. THE ONE MARKER THAT HAS NOT TURNED IS SLEEPING HEART RATE — 66 raw, up from 64, the equal-highest of the last fortnight, nightly low 58, smoothed 63.7 against a baseline of 61.8. So the honest read is a good night sitting on top of an elevated resting state that has not moved since July, and I am weighting it as: the acute cost of Tuesday is paid, the chronic thing underneath it is not. Wrist temperature 35.78, illness flag FALSE. FORM: yesterday's wellness row gives 52.84 − 68.43 = −15.6, down from −12.2, and that is RF6's load 43 landing on top of the class's 46 — arithmetic, not a warning. NONE OF THIS CHANGES TODAY, because today was never going to be decided by a number: the morning is the most expensive of the week and the afternoon is the cheapest, by design. THE CALL IS THE LANDINGS. Sixteen depth jumps is the highest muscle-damage stimulus in the entire week and almost all of that cost is in the drop, so STEP DOWN and rebound rather than dropping — the bar is not the risk, take the complex at the bottom of the band, about 196 lb off your 245. Leg day is four exercises and eight sets in the same visit and it does not grow whatever the class does: belt squat 110 held on purpose, leg extension 100 and leg curl 55 both bumped, tibia raise 20. THEN CRe9 IS SIXTY MINUTES AT 118–165 W AND NOTHING ELSE — no block, no target, nothing to hold, and if it feels like it is doing something it is too hard. Do not upgrade it to Zone 2 because it feels too easy; today is precisely the day it is not for. Hip-flexor work straight after, while you are still warm and well clear of tomorrow morning.

Twenty-four minutes of Zone 3 in six-minute pieces, with recoveries only half as long as the work. That ratio is the instruction: these are meant to be repeatable, not maximal.
Set the number in the first ninety seconds of rep 1, then ride the same number four times. Rep four should be the same wattage as rep one. If it is not, rep one was wrong.
Do not ride the top of the band just because it is available. 248 W is 105% of FTP, and that is where 26 August's CT31 died — 238.9 W with heart rate nine beats over LTHR, and the tune was refused. 222–235 W is where this session lives.
And this ride has a second job. It measures the Zwift FTP offset for yesterday's reference block, and that only happens indoors, on power.
If anything has to give, the plan's cut order takes CCI3's FOURTH rep — three honest six-minute reps at the same 222–248 W, then the fourth rep's time ridden out easy. Same 61 minutes, and the offset still gets measured.
